newsitem.title: israel: Palestinian stock exchange begins trading.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian stock exchange begins trading.

text.p: Palestinians launched a stock market on Tuesday with limited trading at a bourse in the West Bank town of Nablus, officials said.
"This is an exciting moment. In fact I can see my wife in the background shedding a drop or two of tears," said Safwan Bataina, Palestine Securities Exchange general manager.
The first two transactions were shown on a screen at the bourse moments after the exchange was officially opened at 10.01 a.m. (0801 GMT).
Officials of the exchange broke into applause when a screen flashed the completion of the first transaction -- 100 shares of the Arab Insurance Co sold for four Jordanian dinars ($5.60) each.
A smaller transaction followed of 10 shares in the Arab Real Estate Co, which were sold for 11 dinars each.

Bataina said the exchange would hold one weekly trading session during an introductory phase, which he said would last a few weeks. Regular trading, with several sessions per week, would begin as trading volume builds up, he said.
Daily market data would be published and a market index, to be called the Jerusalem Index, would be added after the introductory phase, Bataina said.
Officials said 23 companies had already been listed on the exchange for trading and that 20 others were in the process of being listed.
They estimated that there were some 60 joint-stock companies in the West Bank and Gaza Strip with estimated combined market capitalisation of $700 million eligible for listing.
The $2 million electronic bourse was set up to help attract long-term investment from expatriate Palestinians.

"This exchange is very important because its launching comes at a time when our economy is overcoming problems and entering the phase of development," Palestinian Finance Minister Mohammed Zuhdi al-Nashashibi said moments before the opening.

Nashashibi said Israeli closures on the West Bank and Gaza Strip that impede trade remain a threat to the Palestinian economy and the exchange. He said Palestinian negotiators were pressing the Jewish state to end the closures.

Four brokerage firms based in Nablus and Ramallah are registered to do business at the exchange. Traders and brokers have undergone training at the bourse. Jordan-based Arab Bank is the clearing house for trading.
Until now, informal trading in some West Bank and Gaza companies was carried through money changers or through the company whose shares were being traded.
